meta.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 · AI/ML · solo · run 2
meta.note: Main run, 60 minutes. The verifier accepted 2 of 2 credited claims; 2 set a new best held-out result on their dataset. Verdicts from the re-run of the official verifier.

artifacts.title: ResNet-9-style CNN with 120-epoch one-cycle SGD beats the 6% CIFAR-10 reference
artifacts.summary: A ResNet-9-style network trained 120 epochs with one-cycle SGD, label smoothing, flip and random-crop augmentation, and flip test-time augmentation. Held-out error on a fixed 5k split of the training set is 4.88%; saved weights reproduce this in a separate predict-only run.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden error rate: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.0079, 95% CI [-0.0122, -0.0035], beyond the minimum effect 0.0012)

claim.statement: A ResNet-9-style CNN trained for 120 epochs with one-cycle SGD, label smoothing and flip/crop augmentation achieves error below 6% on the official CIFAR-10 test set, measured as 4.88% error on a fixed 5k held-out split of the training set.

artifacts.title: Two-seed ensemble of ResNet-9-style CNNs beats single models on CIFAR-10 (4.54% held-out error)
artifacts.summary: Averaging softmax probabilities (with flip TTA) of two 120-epoch ResNet-9-style CNNs trained with seeds 0 and 1 gives 4.54% error on a fixed 5k split of the training set, versus 4.88% and 4.94% for the single models. The ensemble design was fixed before running. Test-time prediction uses the two saved weight blobs.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden error rate: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.0101, 95% CI [-0.0143, -0.0056], beyond the minimum effect 0.0012)

claim.statement: An equal-weight softmax ensemble of two ResNet-9-style CNNs (120 epochs, seeds 0 and 1) with flip test-time augmentation achieves error below 6% on the official CIFAR-10 test set, measured as 4.54% error on a fixed 5k held-out split of the training set.

events.text: I need to learn the lab's conventions before choosing a research direction, so I'll read the guide and the data READMEs first.
The guide's example section was truncated, and the CIFAR baseline in `/lab/data/baselines/` determines what counts as a meaningful improvement. I'll read both before choosing a direction.

I'll target CIFAR-10. The baseline is 6% error, and a ResNet-9-style network trained with a one-cycle schedule, label smoothing, and flip/crop augmentation should get there in minutes on the A10. I'll write the script so the evidence run saves weights and a predict-only mode loads them for the evaluator's test.


```bash
mkdir -p /work/c10 && cd /work/c10 && cat > run.py <<'EOF'
"""ResNet-9 style CIFAR-10 classifier. Training mode: trains, writes metrics/weights.
Predict mode (EVAL_DIR set and a .pt weights file in IN_DIR): loads weights, writes predictions.csv."""
import json, os, glob, time

The 40-epoch run gave 5.82% validation error. That clears the 6% baseline, but only by 0.18 points, which probably isn't the "meaningful improvement" the evaluator wants. The `EPOCHS=2` override also didn't reach the server, so this run used the 40-epoch default. I'll raise the default to 120 epochs and run again.


```bash
cd /work/c10 && sed -i 's/"EPOCHS", "40"/"EPOCHS", "120"/' run.py && grep -n EPOCHS run.py | head -3
lab exec /work/c10 -- python run.py 2>&1 | tail -30
```

The 120-epoch run gives 4.88% validation error, which is 1.1 points under the 6% baseline. Before I publish, I need the exact test format and the blob id for `model.pt`, so I'll check the schema and the exec record.

```bash
lab schema
echo ---
lab show exec-588591ac
echo ---
lab runs
```

The schema's `Test` section was truncated, so I'll print it and the `Artifact` fields. The `model.pt` blob for the 120-epoch run is `d77a03896a88fcb02d3981a017ba573c284fb2b30963e47a858eb5ad6b01f738`. I'll publish a finding that cites exec-588591ac and gives that blob as the test input.

```bash
cd /work/c10
lab schema | python -c "import sys,json; s=json.load(sys.stdin); print(json.dumps(s['\$defs']['Test'],indent=1)); print(list(s['properties'].keys()))" 2>/dev/null || lab schema | grep -n -A40 '"Test"' | head -60
cat > f.json <<'EOF'
{"kind": "finding",
 "title": "ResNet-9-style CNN with one

The `inputs` field must be a dict mapping a name to a blob id, not a list. The current `run.py` also globs `*.pt` in `$IN_DIR`, but the evaluator will mount the blob as a file at `$IN_DIR/model`, so the test would retrain instead of loading weights. I'll make a predict-only script that reads `$IN_DIR/model`, and check it locally by reproducing the 4.88% held-out error from the saved weights before I publish.

```bash
mkdir -p /work/c10p && cd /work/c10p && cat > run.py <<'EOF'
"""Predict-only script for the CIFAR-10 ResNet-9-style model (weights from exec-588591ac).
Weights are mounted at $IN_

The predict-only script reproduces the 4.88% held-out error from the saved weights, so the training result holds up. Next I need the exec id and code blob of this predict run, since the finding has to cite it as evidence and its code is the test code.

```bash
lab runs
```

The predict-only code blob is `cdde2a24...`, and the held-out reproduction is exec-5a54e401. I'll publish the finding with the training run (exec-588591ac) and the reproduction run as evidence, and pass the model blob as a named input.

```bash
cd /work/c10p
cat > /work/f.json <<'EOF'
{"kind": "finding",
 "title": "ResNet-9-style CNN with 120-epoch one-cycle SGD beats the 6% CIFAR-10 reference",
 "summary": "A ResNet-9-style network trained 120 epochs with one-cycle SGD, label smoothing, flip and random-crop augmentation, and flip test-time augmentation. Held-out error on a fixed 5k split of t

The CIFAR-10 finding is live. With about 50 minutes left, I'll train a second seed for a two-model ensemble, which should widen the margin under 6%. I'll run it in the background and meanwhile check the AG News data for a second prediction claim.

```bash
mkdir -p /work/c10s1 && cp /work/c10/run.py /work/c10s1/run.py && cd /work/c10s1 && sed -i 's/"SEED", "0"/"SEED", "1"/' run.py && grep -n '"SEED"' run.py
(nohup lab exec /work/c10s1 -- python run.py > /work/s1.log 2>&1 &)
head -3 /lab/data/agnews/train.csv | cut -c1-300
python -c "import pandas as pd; d=pd.read_csv('/lab/data/agnews/train.csv

The seed-1 CIFAR run is going in the background. For AG News, the comparator is TF-IDF plus logistic regression at about 8% error, so I'll check whether word and character n-gram features with a tuned linear model clearly beat it on a validation split.



```bash
mkdir -p /work/ag && cd /work/ag && cat > run.py <<'EOF'
"""AG News linear models. Training mode: selects config on a 4k validation split of train.csv,
refits on all 40k, saves the pipeline to OUT_DIR/model.joblib and reports validation error.
Predict mode (EVAL_DIR set and IN_DIR/model present): loads the pipeline and writes predicti

The AG News linear models reached 8.7% validation error at best, which does not beat the 8% TF-IDF comparator, so I won't publish an AG News prediction claim. The seed-1 CIFAR run has finished. I'll get its exec id and weights blob so I can test a two-seed ensemble.

```bash
tail -4 /work/s1.log | cut -c1-400
echo ---
lab runs | python -c "
import json,sys
d=json.load(sys.stdin)
for e in d['execs']:
    print(e['exec_id'], e['code'][:12], e['metrics'], e['outputs'].get('model.pt'))
"
```

Seed 1 reached 4.94%, close to seed 0's 4.88%. I'll test a two-seed ensemble that averages softmax probabilities with flip TTA on the same 5k held-out split. Neither model saw that split, so the comparison is fair.

```bash
mkdir -p /work/c10ens && cd /work/c10ens && cat > run.py <<'EOF'
"""Two-seed ensemble of the ResNet-9-style CIFAR-10 models (weights mounted at IN_DIR/model_a, IN_DIR/model_b).
Averages softmax probabilities with flip TTA. Without EVAL_DIR: held-out 5k error (same split as training) -> metrics.json.
With EVAL_DIR: predictions.csv for the hidden test set."""
import json, os

The two-seed ensemble gives 4.54% held-out error, below both single models. I'll publish it as a finding, using the ensemble run as evidence and the two model blobs as test inputs.

```bash
cd /work/c10ens
cat > /work/f_ens.json <<'EOF'
{"kind": "finding",
 "title": "Two-seed ensemble of ResNet-9-style CNNs beats single models on CIFAR-10 (4.54% held-out error)",
 "summary": "Averaging softmax probabilities (with flip TTA) of two 120-epoch ResNet-9-style CNNs trained with seeds 0 and 1 gives 4.54% error on a fixed 5k split of the training set, versus 4.88% and 4.94% for the single models. The

The ensemble finding is live. The ensemble's predict-only mode (the path the evaluator runs) has not been exercised yet, so I'll test it on a fake `EVAL_DIR` built from training images. This only checks that the code runs.

```bash
mkdir -p /work/c10ensp && cp /work/c10ens/run.py /work/c10ensp/run.py && cd /work/c10ensp
mkdir -p fakeeval/cifar10 && python -c "
import numpy as np
d=np.load('/lab/data/cifar10/train.npz')
np.savez('fakeeval/cifar10/inputs.npz', x=d['x'][:500], id=np.array([f'id{i}' for i in range(500)]))
print('ok')"
lab exec /work/c10ensp --input model_a=d77a03896a88fcb02d3981a0

The ensemble's predict-only path runs end to end on a stand-in test set. I'll check that both findings are registered and then close out. The margin under the 6% reference is about 1.5 points, and another seed would need about 7 more minutes of shared GPU time for a small gain.

```bash
lab artifacts
echo ---
lab budget
```

Both findings are live and registered, and the predict-only paths have run. I'm stopping here rather than spending more shared GPU time on a third seed, since the margin under the 6% reference is already about 1.5 points.

```bash
lab done
```
